scenes.title: IAM: Identity & Access Management
scenes.narration: Identity and Access Management controls who can do what in your cloud account, and getting it right is the foundation of cloud security.

scenes.title: The Core Pieces
bullets: Users and roles represent identities that make requests to cloud services.
Policies are documents that grant or deny specific actions on specific resources.
Roles let services and applications assume temporary permissions without long-lived keys.
scenes.narration: IAM revolves around identities such as users and roles that call cloud APIs. Policies are JSON documents that spell out exactly which actions are allowed on which resources. Roles are especially powerful because they grant temporary credentials, letting services act securely without hardcoded keys.

scenes.title: How a Request Is Evaluated
scenes.narration: Every API call passes through IAM's evaluation logic. The service collects all policies attached to the identity and the resource. Any explicit deny immediately blocks the request, and without a matching allow the default is denial. Understanding this order explains most access puzzles.

scenes.title: A Least-Privilege IAM Policy
scenes.narration: This policy demonstrates least privilege, granting only read access and only to one bucket's raw prefix. The Action list names the exact operations allowed, and the Resource list scopes them tightly to specific ARNs. By granting the minimum needed rather than broad wildcards, you dramatically shrink the blast radius of any leaked credential.

scenes.title: Broad vs. Least Privilege
scenes.narration: Granting broad wildcard access feels convenient but turns any compromised key into a catastrophe. Least privilege instead grants only the actions and resources actually required. It takes more thought upfront, yet it is the single most effective habit for cloud security.

scenes.text: Grant the least privilege necessary and prefer temporary roles over long-lived keys — tight IAM is the difference between a minor incident and a breach.
scenes.narration: Least privilege and short-lived roles are the heart of cloud security. When permissions are tightly scoped, a leaked credential becomes a small problem instead of a company-wide breach.
